opportunities.title: National Lotteries Commission – Arts and Culture Sector
opportunities.description: Funds the development of the arts and the preservation of South African culture and national heritage, including natural environmental heritage, historical and architectural heritage. Empowers communities and enables artists to showcase work internationally.
opportunities.eligibility: South African registered non-profit organisations working in arts and culture
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply via the NLC portal at https://www.nlcsa.org.za/arts-and-culture/

opportunities.title: BASA Supporting Grants Programme
opportunities.description: Funded by the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture. Provides matching grants to support partnerships between business and the arts sector in South Africa, building organisational sustainability.
opportunities.eligibility: Arts organisations with confirmed business sponsorship
opportunities.how_to_apply: Contact BASA at info@basa.co.za or visit www.basa.co.za

opportunities.title: Arts & Culture Trust (ACT) Development Grants
opportunities.description: ACT has served the arts and culture sector across all 9 provinces for 31 years through development and grant making. Founded in 1994 with support from Nedcor Bank and Sun International.
opportunities.eligibility: South African arts and culture practitioners and organisations across all 9 provinces
opportunities.how_to_apply: Visit https://act.org.za/ for current application information

opportunities.title: DSAC Open Tenders
opportunities.funder: Department of Sport, Arts and Culture
opportunities.description: The Department of Sport, Arts and Culture regularly publishes tenders for service provision related to arts and culture infrastructure, programmes, and services.
opportunities.eligibility: Registered service providers meeting specific tender requirements
opportunities.how_to_apply: Check https://www.dsac.gov.za/qt-tenders and https://www.etenders.gov.za/ regularly

opportunities.title: The African Arts Trust Grants
opportunities.description: Grant making concentrated on Eastern and Southern Africa, supporting the development of arts across the continent.
opportunities.eligibility: Arts organisations and practitioners in Eastern and Southern Africa
opportunities.how_to_apply: Visit https://www.theafricanartstrust.org/funding-developing-arts-africa.php

opportunities.title: Electric South – Immersive & New Media Grants
opportunities.description: Backs African artists making virtual reality, augmented reality and immersive/interactive non-fiction — from prototype through to completion — via the New Dimensions Lab and completion grants. Premiered at Venice VR, Sundance New Frontier and IDFA DocLab.
opportunities.eligibility: African artists, storytellers and teams working in VR/AR/XR and digital storytelling
opportunities.how_to_apply: Watch https://electricsouth.org for open lab and grant calls

opportunities.title: Pulitzer Center – Underreported Story Grants
opportunities.description: Grants covering the hard costs of ambitious, underreported journalism — including audio/podcast, documentary and multimedia — with a dedicated Africa reporting track. South African journalists and storytellers are eligible.
opportunities.eligibility: Individual journalists, storytellers and newsrooms (South Africa eligible)
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply via https://pulitzercenter.org/grants-fellowships

opportunities.title: Content is Queen – Podcast Micro-Grants
opportunities.description: Monthly micro-grants plus mentoring to help creators develop and produce podcast episodes or pilots. Open to applicants worldwide, including South Africa.
opportunities.eligibility: Individual podcasters, 18+, worldwide
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply via https://contentisqueen.org

opportunities.title: Institute for Creative Arts (ICA) Fellowships & Live Art
opportunities.description: Fellowships and commissions for interdisciplinary, live and public-space art — including the biennial ICA Live Art Festival and Infecting the City. A strong home for experimental, site-responsive and socially-engaged practice.
opportunities.eligibility: Individual artists and researchers (SA / Africa-based; some international fellowships)
opportunities.how_to_apply: See open calls and fellowship windows at https://humanities.uct.ac.za/ica

opportunities.title: Art Moves Africa – Mobility Fund
opportunities.description: Travel grants enabling artists and cultural operators to move within Africa for research, residencies, festivals, training and collaboration.
opportunities.eligibility: Artists, curators and cultural operators living and working in Africa
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply during open rounds at https://artmovesafrica.org

opportunities.title: National Film & Video Foundation (NFVF) Funding
opportunities.description: South Africa's statutory screen funder: development, production, marketing and distribution funding, plus bursaries for film study and training.
opportunities.eligibility: South African filmmakers and production companies (orgs majority black-owned); individuals for training and bursaries
opportunities.how_to_apply: See current calls at https://www.nfvf.co.za

opportunities.title: Prince Claus Fund – Awards, Seed & Mentorship
opportunities.description: Supports emerging artists and cultural practitioners doing socially and politically engaged work, through Seed Awards, Mentorship Awards and mobility/building programmes. Global South including South Africa.
opportunities.eligibility: Emerging artists and cultural practitioners (1–10 years), Global South incl. SA
opportunities.how_to_apply: See current calls at https://princeclausfund.nl/awards-and-programmes

opportunities.title: Africa No Filter – Storytelling Grants
opportunities.description: Grants to shift African narratives — supporting storytellers, media and creatives working in digital, audio and new-media storytelling (Kekere micro-grants, Story Labs and project support).
opportunities.eligibility: Individual storytellers and organisations across Africa (some calls under-35)
opportunities.how_to_apply: See open calls at https://africanofilter.org/our-grants

opportunities.title: Pro Helvetia Johannesburg – Co-creation, Mobility & Residency
opportunities.description: The Swiss Arts Council's Southern Africa office funds collaboration, research, mobility and interdisciplinary/digital projects between Switzerland and Southern Africa, plus an annual residency.
opportunities.eligibility: Individuals, collectives and organisations (a Swiss + Southern/E/W/Central African partner for co-creation)
opportunities.how_to_apply: See guidelines and calls at https://johannesburg.prohelvetia.org

opportunities.title: IDFA Bertha Fund – Creative Documentary
opportunities.description: Supports author-driven creative documentary by filmmakers from under-resourced regions, including South Africa (subject to the annual country list).
opportunities.eligibility: Director + producer teams from eligible countries (SA typically eligible)
opportunities.how_to_apply: See https://professionals.idfa.nl/training-funding/funding/about-the-idfa-bertha-fund/

opportunities.title: Sundance Institute Documentary Fund
opportunities.description: Unrestricted grants and labs for nonfiction filmmakers worldwide, including South Africa, from development through post-production.
opportunities.eligibility: Individual nonfiction filmmakers worldwide (SA eligible)
opportunities.how_to_apply: See open windows at https://www.sundance.org/programs/documentary-fund

opportunities.title: Sasol New Signatures Art Competition
opportunities.amount: R100,000 first prize + Pretoria Art Museum solo exhibition
opportunities.description: South Africa's longest-running national art competition for emerging artists, with cash prizes and a solo exhibition for the winner.
opportunities.eligibility: South African citizens/permanent residents, 18+, not previously solo-exhibited or gallery-represented
opportunities.how_to_apply: Enter via https://www.sasolsignatures.co.za/

opportunities.title: Absa L'Atelier Art Competition
opportunities.funder: Absa / SANAVA / French Institute of South Africa
opportunities.amount: Cash awards + residencies (SA / France), incl. the Gérard Sekoto Award
opportunities.description: Pan-African emerging-artist competition offering cash and residency awards, including the Gérard Sekoto Award for a South African artist.
opportunities.eligibility: Emerging artists from participating African countries (incl. SA)
opportunities.how_to_apply: See https://www.absa.africa/absa-latelier-2026/

opportunities.title: The Ampersand Foundation Fellowship
opportunities.amount: Funded 1–2 month New York residency fellowship
opportunities.description: A funded New York (Tribeca) residency fellowship for professional South African contemporary visual artists.
opportunities.eligibility: Professional South African contemporary visual artists
opportunities.how_to_apply: See https://www.theampersandfoundation.com/how-to-apply

opportunities.title: Tierney Fellowship (Photography)
opportunities.funder: Market Photo Workshop / Tierney Family Foundation
opportunities.description: A fellowship for emerging South African photographers to produce a new photographic body of work with year-long mentorship, via partner institutions.
opportunities.eligibility: Emerging photographers via SA partner institutions (Market Photo Workshop, Wits, Michaelis)
opportunities.how_to_apply: See https://marketphotoworkshop.co.za/projects/mentorships-residencies/tierney-fellowship/

opportunities.title: Pollock-Krasner Foundation Grants
opportunities.description: Need-based project/working grants to professional visual artists worldwide, including South Africa. Painters, sculptors and artists working on paper.
opportunities.eligibility: Professional, actively-exhibiting visual artists worldwide (SA eligible)
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply (rolling) via https://www.pkf.org/apply/how-to-apply/

opportunities.title: African Culture Fund – SOFACO Organisational Structuring Support
opportunities.description: Through the Solidarity Fund for Artists and Cultural Organisations (SOFACO), ACF awards professional grants to strengthen the structures of African cultural organisations — strategic planning, fundraising, governance, M&E, restructuring and internal capacity building. Open to organisations across Africa, including South Africa.
opportunities.eligibility: Legally registered cultural organisations based in Africa with at least 3 years of proven activity and a physical address in an African country
opportunities.how_to_apply: Complete the SOFACO application form from the ACF site and email it as a PDF to applications@africanculturefund.net and administrator@africanculturefund.net (English or French). Watch for the current call on the ACF website.

opportunities.title: Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture – Mobility Grants
opportunities.description: Mobility grants supporting short-term travel for individual artists and cultural professionals — both intra-African (Africa–Africa) and intercontinental (Africa–Europe) — for collaboration, research, networking and career development. Run under the EU/Goethe-Institut Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture programme with quarterly cut-off dates (next: 15 September 2026).
opportunities.eligibility: Individual artists and cultural professionals (18+) based in Sub-Saharan Africa (incl. South Africa) or the EU, working across artistic disciplines
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online via the Goethe Application Portal (GAP); next cut-off 15 September 2026. See https://www.goethe.de/prj/aep/en/cal/ssa/mga.html

opportunities.title: British Council – Connections Through Culture Grants
opportunities.description: Grants for fresh cultural partnerships between the UK and South Africa — helping artists, collectives, festivals, hubs and cultural organisations develop new collaborations and exchange at any stage. Each project pairs at least one UK-based partner with a South African partner; delivery runs Dec 2026–Dec 2027.
opportunities.eligibility: Creative practitioners, artists, collectives and cultural organisations based in South Africa, partnering with at least one UK-based collaborator
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online during the open round at https://arts.britishcouncil.org/connections-through-culture (applications close 12 August 2026, 23:59 BST).

opportunities.title: Spier Light Art 2027 – Open Call for Proposals
opportunities.funder: Spier Arts Trust / Spier Light Art
opportunities.description: South Africa's leading platform for light-based contemporary art — Africa's longest-running exhibition of its kind, now in its ninth year. Commissions site-specific, sculptural, interactive, digital, video, sound and light-based works for the Spier Wine Farm in Stellenbosch (exhibition 26 Feb–21 Mar 2027). Light must be central to the concept, medium and subject. The 2027 edition's expression-of-interest call closed on 21 July 2026; this flagship annual open call typically reopens around mid-year, so the next call is expected ~mid-2027.
opportunities.eligibility: Artists, designers, collectives, students and institutions from diverse backgrounds, disciplines and career stages
opportunities.how_to_apply: The 2027 call closed 21 July 2026. Watch spierlightart.co.za for the next annual open call (~mid-2027).

opportunities.title: National Arts Council – Annual Project Funding
opportunities.description: The NAC's core annual grant for South African arts practitioners and organisations across all disciplines — craft, dance, literature, music, theatre, visual arts and multidiscipline. Projects must address at least two of six focus areas: social cohesion, marginalised/indigenous arts, social issues, vulnerable groups, innovation/digital arts, and skills/entrepreneurship. Annual cycle (2026–2027 round closed 13 March 2026; next expected Jan–Feb 2027).
opportunities.eligibility: Individual arts practitioners, registered arts organisations and community art centres in South Africa, active in any arts discipline
opportunities.how_to_apply: Register and apply online at https://nac.praxisgms.co.za/ during the open call (watch for next cycle announcement around Jan 2027).

opportunities.title: DSAC – Mzansi Golden Economy (MGE) Grant
opportunities.funder: Department of Sport, Arts and Culture (DSAC)
opportunities.description: South Africa's largest single competitive arts grant. DSAC's Mzansi Golden Economy programme funds Cultural and Creative Industries Projects (CCIPs) and Touring Ventures, with individual grants of up to R2 million. Open to SA-citizen-owned arts, culture and heritage NPOs and Pty Ltd companies. Annual open call, typically December to January. 2025/26 round (projects May 2026–Feb 2027) closed 1 February 2026; next call expected December 2026.
opportunities.eligibility: SA-citizen-owned and managed arts, culture and heritage NPOs or Pty Ltd companies, tax-compliant with independent legal status
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply via https://www.eservices.gov.za during the annual open call. Watch https://www.dsac.gov.za for the 2026/27 call (~December 2026).

opportunities.title: Goethe-Institut Project Space (GPS) – Rural Arts Grant
opportunities.amount: Up to R100,000 per project (3 projects selected annually)
opportunities.description: Annual seed grants for artistic projects engaging communities in rural and peri-urban parts of South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini. Projects must be realised outside the major urban centres (not solely Joburg, Cape Town or Durban) and focus on producing or facilitating artistic content with local communities or arts spaces. 2026 cycle projects are currently in implementation; next call for 2027 projects expected around September 2026.
opportunities.eligibility: Arts professionals based in South Africa, Lesotho or Eswatini proposing community-engaged projects in rural or peri-urban settings
opportunities.how_to_apply: Submit applications by email to gpsapplications@goethe.de during the annual open call. Watch https://www.goethe.de/ins/za for the 2027 call (~Sept 2026).

opportunities.title: Nirox Foundation – International Artist Residency
opportunities.amount: Fully funded (studio, accommodation and material support)
opportunities.description: Funded residency programme at Nirox Sculpture Park in the Cradle of Humankind World Heritage Site, Gauteng — one of South Africa's most significant contemporary art venues. Open to visual artists, sculptors and interdisciplinary practitioners from anywhere in the world. Residency period: January–June 2027. The biosphere and outdoor environment are central to the programme.
opportunities.eligibility: Individual visual artists, sculptors and interdisciplinary practitioners worldwide (international and SA applicants welcome)
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply via Res Artis (resartis.org) or contact the Nirox Foundation directly. See the listing at https://resartis.org/listings/artist-in-residence-south-africa-npo-243-824/

opportunities.title: Standard Bank Young Artist Awards
opportunities.amount: Cash prize + full production budget + National Arts Festival platform
opportunities.description: South Africa's most prestigious emerging-artist award, established 1981. Five artists across different disciplines are selected annually and supported to create and present new work at the National Arts Festival in Makhanda. Winners receive a cash prize, production funding, marketing support and national recognition throughout the award year. 2026 winners announced April 2026. Nominations for 2027 expected to open August 2026. Self-nominations not accepted.
opportunities.eligibility: South African artists aged 35 or under, nominated by peers or institutions (no self-nominations), not previously SBYA winners
opportunities.how_to_apply: Nominations via nationalartsfestival.co.za (nomination call opens ~August each year).

opportunities.title: Western Cape – Arts, Culture and Heritage Funding
opportunities.funder: Western Cape Dept of Cultural Affairs and Sport
opportunities.description: Annual provincial grants for arts, culture and heritage initiatives in the Western Cape, open to registered arts organisations, individual artists and events companies. Projects may span any discipline and must promote inclusion, innovation, gender equality, skills development or social cohesion. Funding period: 1 April–31 March. 2026/27 round closed 9 March 2026; next call expected December 2026.
opportunities.eligibility: SA citizens based in the Western Cape — registered arts, culture and heritage organisations, individual artists and events companies
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply via the Western Cape Government arts funding portal at westerncape.gov.za/cas (watch for next call around December 2026).

opportunities.title: Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture – Visual Art Collaboration Grant
opportunities.description: Supports collaborative visual arts projects between teams in Sub-Saharan Africa (including South Africa) and Europe, covering production costs, cross-border creative exchange, exhibition and dissemination. The team lead must be based in Sub-Saharan Africa; minimum two-person teams of visual artists, curators, digital media artists or cultural managers. Project duration: 12 months (July 2026–July 2027). Under the EU-funded Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture (AEPC) programme — distinct from the mobility grants in the same programme.
opportunities.eligibility: Teams of 2+ visual arts practitioners (18+) with a Sub-Saharan Africa-based team lead and at least one European partner
opportunities.how_to_apply: Applications via the Goethe-Institut GAP Portal (now closed). Watch https://www.goethe.de/prj/aep for the next call.

opportunities.title: University of Johannesburg – Artists in Residence Programme
opportunities.amount: Studio space and programme support (varies per arrangement)
opportunities.description: A rolling artist-in-residence programme at the University of Johannesburg, welcoming emerging and established artists from across the globe, with preference for those linked to Africa. Both physical (on-campus studio) and remote residency formats are available. Artists engage with UJ students, faculty and the broader Joburg arts community during their stay.
opportunities.eligibility: Emerging and established individual artists from anywhere in the world; preference for African-linked practitioners
opportunities.how_to_apply: See the On the Move listing and contact UJ directly. Both physical and remote applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

opportunities.title: eThekwini Municipality – Arts and Culture Grant-in-Aid
opportunities.description: Annual Grant-in-Aid from the eThekwini Municipality's Recreation and Parks Directorate for non-profit performing arts and cultural organisations operating within the eThekwini Metro (Durban area). Projects must be scheduled between April and June of the funding year. A key source of municipal arts support for KwaZulu-Natal organisations. 2025/26 call closed February 2026.
opportunities.eligibility: Registered NPOs and NPCs in the performing arts and cultural sector with programmes and activities within the eThekwini Municipality
opportunities.how_to_apply: Application forms available from ethekwini.gov.za or by email from the municipality. Watch for the next annual call around November 2026.
